A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same LLM-SR research work. All 29 pages of each version, including equations, tables, figures, references, and Appendices A–E, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original equation-discovery experiments, numerical benchmark comparisons in Table 1, ablations in Section 5.1, and additional empirical analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark results, ablations, discovered equations, and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: Section 2, Algorithms 1–2, and Appendix B retain the same hypothesis generation, parameter optimization, fitness assessment, and experience-buffer procedures. The abstract's revised terminology introduces no method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same two custom oscillator problems, synthetic E. coli growth problem, and aluminum stress-strain data. The Feynman benchmark analysis in Appendix C and ID/OOD coverage are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains GPlearn, DSR, uDSR, and PySR. Comparator membership also remains unchanged in the ablation and qualitative comparisons.

E3.justification: The model backbones, NMSE metric, ID/OOD evaluation, data partitions, and search budgets are unchanged. Sections 3.2–3.3 still describe over 2M baseline iterations and 2.5K LLM-SR iterations; Appendix D retains the same dataset settings.

E4.justification: Section 5.1 retains the problem-specification, iterative-refinement, coefficient-optimization, and optimizer ablations. Appendices C and E retain the same memorization analysis, search trajectories, and qualitative case studies.

E5.justification: Appendix A.1 retains the statement that each SR baseline was executed five times, and Appendix A.2 retains best-result reporting for LLM-SR. No seed information, uncertainty estimates, or statistical testing practices are added or removed.

E6.justification: Table 1's values are identical; for example, GPT-3.5 LLM-SR's Oscillation 2 ID/OOD NMSE remains 2.12e-7/3.81e-5. The ablation values, discovered equations, performance trajectories, and appendix findings are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 2's mathematical formulation and scoring definitions, Appendix B's sampling formulas, and Appendix D's benchmark equations are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: v2 adds an abstract sentence about more efficient search through scientific prior knowledge, but v1 already makes this claim in its introduction, contribution list, and Section 4.3. The method, accuracy, generalization, and efficiency claims retain their scope.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same explanations involving scientific priors and iterative refinement, the Feynman memorization discussion, and the Appendix E numerical-differentiation edge case. Section 7's computational-cost and unreliable-prior-knowledge limitations are unchanged.

D1.justification: The code-access statement and technical disclosures in Sections 3.3 and Appendices A–D are unchanged, including sampling parameters, island structure, execution limits, parallel evaluators, prompts, and data-generation details.

R1.justification: Section 6 and the reference list retain the same works and positioning relative to symbolic regression, FunSearch, and LLM-based optimization. Naming symbolic regression in the abstract repeats terminology already established in v1.

P1.justification: The abstract now explicitly identifies equation discovery as symbolic regression, calls proposed skeletons hypotheses, and summarizes the existing efficiency finding. Review-status headers are removed; the remaining prose and section organization are retained apart from text reflow.

P2.justification: Figure 5 moves from page 10 to 11 and Figure 6 from page 11 to 12, with accompanying text reflow and header removal. All 23 figure images and their captions remain unchanged, as do both tables' contents and structures.

improvement.justification: v2 offers modest presentation gains: the abstract clarifies terminology and summarizes the existing efficiency finding, while relocating Figure 5 restores Figure 4–5 display order and places the ablation figure within its discussion. The scientific evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations remain unchanged, so the improvement is limited to communication.
